season.evidence: Stored Jul-Sep with Oct larch colour; web: WTA class 3 hike, late-May trip found mushy snow slopes, late-August and September scrambles dry, larches in fall, spring road closures; log histogram peaks Jul and Sep.

track.why: Only one route is stored on the peak. Logged South Slope; the track starts 5 m from our trailhead pin, ends 26 m away, summit 5 m; the report describes the basin camp, scree up the south slope and the exposed class 3 move to the summit; Sept 3 is in season.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Complete July 4 track but no report or route name; second choice.
Sept 1 South route complete, started from a camp, no report text.
Logged Saska Pass; may be a link-up.
June 20 S face ski/snow track, not complete.

facts.text: The summit cone is loose, shattered rock and dirt; the exposed class 3 step to the summit chimney is the one spot worth a careful look.
A stable stair-like scree line in a dry gully at the bottom of the slope gives the easiest early footing.
In early September the basin below the col has a camp with running water and dense larches; scree on the way down is fast to boot-ski.
In mid-September a fresh storm can plaster the upper rock with snow, so expect it slower and give it time to melt.

notes: The packet has one catalog route, so I accepted the one-route rule for 2300001. The track appears to climb the south scree slope rather than strictly the col line; the stored title says via the Emerald-Saska col, which may be the Emerald traverse and not the normal south route.
